A1.justification: The PDFs describe the same research despite the changed title and format. The shared model, principal theorems, figures, and matched appendix proofs establish continuity. Both versions provide readable material sufficient for comparison, including their appendices.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B report original synthetic experiments on classification accuracy, outlier placement, attention scores, and gating behavior.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C report original synthetic and SST-2 experiments, including attention comparisons, training interventions, and PCA-based classification results.

M1.justification: The core binary-classification model and SGD algorithm remain unchanged. Appendix C.1 adds a training variant that switches from randomly positioned outliers to outliers closest to the query halfway through training. Appendices H–I also sketch multi-head multiclass and squared-loss regression adaptations.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates synthetic binary-classification tasks. v2 retains that coverage and adds SST-2 sentiment classification with phrase-trigger outliers, plus classification using reduced sentence representations. The multiclass and regression appendices do not report additional empirical tasks.

E2.justification: v1 compares Mamba against linear Transformers. v2 adds an evaluated three-layer softmax Transformer to the synthetic placement comparison in Table 3 and compares softmax and linear attention across corruption levels in Tables 4–5. This substantially broadens the comparator family.

E3.justification: The new SST-2 protocol uses eight context examples, three-layer models with two heads, and training/test outlier rates of 0.25/0.75. Appendix C introduces synthetic comparisons with dimension 72, head counts from one to four, and staged training. v1's original synthetic placement study used dimension 30, so its scores are not directly comparable to the revised comparison.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's attention/gating visualizations and positional robustness study, v2 adds head-count sensitivity, softmax-versus-linear robustness sweeps, a training intervention targeting the closest-to-query failure case, and PCA classification experiments examining the representation assumptions.

E5.justification: The retained plots, including their error bars and shading, are unchanged. Neither version specifies empirical seed counts or repeated-run counts, and the added tables report point estimates without introducing confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results, including SST-2 FQ accuracies of 74.10% for Mamba and 70.18% for linear attention. The synthetic CQ comparison changes from 73.28%/78.60% in v1 Table 1 to 82.73%/93.96% in v2 Table 3, which also reports 99.28% for softmax attention. These are results under changed settings, not established same-setting improvements. The original plotted results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 adds mutual orthogonality of training outliers. Theorem 2 expands test outliers by adding an orthogonal residual and removes the unit-norm restriction. Appendices H–I add a multiclass reduction and squared-loss gradient derivations. The existing proofs are essentially unchanged; notably, Appendix E.2 still uses the earlier span-only outlier formulation.

C1.justification: The abstract and three principal contributions retain the central claims about Mamba's learnability, gating-based outlier suppression, and robustness relative to the analyzed linear Transformer. The added one-layer/single-head wording makes the existing comparator setting explicit, while the new experiments support the retained claims.

C2.justification: Remark 6 adds substantive qualifications about the restricted Transformer comparison and robustness of larger Transformers. Remark 8 explains Equation 18 as a decaying lower bound on gating values. The conclusion explicitly discusses orthogonality and single-layer limitations, while Appendix C interprets softmax robustness, head-count sensitivity, and mitigation of positional failures.

D1.justification: v2 supplies implementation details for the added studies: SST-2 prompt and trigger construction, DistilBERT sentence representations and PCA dimensions, and the timing of the training curriculum switch. The original SGD pseudocode and initialization remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds concurrent Mamba work by Oh et al. (2025), distinguishing its fixed gating from this paper's trainable gating. v2 also adds relevant context-hijacking, recency, dataset, and embedding references. These are focused additions rather than a wholesale change in research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 retitles the paper, revises explanatory passages and the conclusion, consolidates synthetic experiments, and separates related work, algorithms, and extensions into clearer appendix sections. Most existing scientific prose and proof text are retained.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column formatting, with substantial rearrangement of figures and tables. Figures 1–6 retain their graphics but receive placement, sizing, and caption changes; several empirical tables are added. Tables 4–5 have incomplete alpha headers, and Table 5's softmax heading conflicts with its linear-attention caption.

improvement.justification: SST-2 evaluation, softmax controls, and clearer limitations strengthen empirical relevance and interpretation. However, Theorem 2 adds an orthogonal residual that the retained Appendix E.2 proof does not address. The new squared-loss gating gradient in Equation 204 also has the opposite sign to the derivative implied by Equation 3. These theoretical reliability issues make the net effect of the empirical and explanatory gains uncertain.
